outcome.technical: F644. In the P125.30-0h5 tree: (1) drive-phase.py's apply_answer now records the operator's --answer retry --reason, keyed by _mark to the NEW attempt's start (read after start_task re-stamps it via a reload through load_phase), under state's retryReason map for the task id, holding the start and the value. (2) audit-lookup.py's compose_executor_brief Retry section now reads that via a new retry_reason(ctx, phase, task) helper (a drive_state lookup, start-gated) and prints the operator's reason for the retry, or none recorded. (3) The Retry section's outcome.technical and redFirst are now read from the prior attempt's actual filed return via a new previous_filed_return(ctx, task, role) helper, which lists the task's own evidence returns directory and picks the newest filename whose start key sorts strictly before the current attempt's start key (ISO timestamps sort lexicographically, so this is chronological), rather than from task.outcome/task.redFirst - those manifest fields only move at audit-task.py's close_task (done), so a retried, never-closed attempt left them exactly as an earlier close left them, which is why P125.1's real retry brief printed none recorded over a filed return that had proved its red-first. (4) red_step_lines no longer joins a red step's recorded failing list into one string and re-excerpts it through _excerpt.reason_of (a second, tighter truncation on top of run-test-gate.py's own MAX_FAILING bound of ten) - it now prints every already-recorded failing line verbatim, one per line, so a failing file further back in the list is never collapsed behind a bare plus-N-more count. Proved red-first: ran python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py --selftest on HEAD's code (before this fix) with the new bf53/bf53a/bf54/bf55 cases added - 91 of 95 cases passed, the 4 new ones failing exactly as expected (bf53: no reason line at all; bf54: the sweep excerpt dropped the deep FAIL line behind a plus-3-more count; bf55: none recorded printed over a filed redFirst and technical). Re-ran after applying the fix: 95 of 95 passed. Also updated the pre-existing bf3 fixture, which had set task.outcome.technical directly with no filed return - a shape that cannot occur in production, since that field only ever moves at close_task - so it now files an executor return at the retried attempt's own earlier start instead, which is what the fixed Retry section reads. Full-repo sweep after the fix: tools/sweep-selftests.py --jobs 6 reported every file ok with zero FAIL lines. plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest passed in full, the retry-answer paths unaffected beyond the new state write. No manifest file touched; gates is empty because this task's own-tests command is exactly the command given after the double-dash, already run and reported here.
outcome.descriptive: A retry brief now quotes the operator's own --reason, names every failing line a red sweep step recorded instead of a doubly-truncated snippet, and reads the retried attempt's actual filed return for outcome.technical/redFirst instead of the never-updated task fields.

testsAdded: bf53: a retry brief over an attempt whose answer carried --reason prints that reason verbatim in the retry section
bf54: a retry brief over a red sweep step names each failing file's own FAIL <case> lines, not only the step's tail
bf55: a retry brief over an attempt whose filed return carries a proved redFirst prints it, never 'none recorded'

redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 2, but its output carries no test tally this command reads, so an assertion failure cannot be told from a crash - no test is known to have been collected: no tally or error reader matched its output, so no line of it is quoted as decisive; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)
